rationale: Unsigned SMB sessions allow relay and tampering on the flat hotel LAN, so network and configuration hardening is the control gap.
Link local name resolution is an unneeded default function that enables credential capture, so it belongs in the hardening baseline.

family: Untrusted, self signed, weak or expired certificates
rationale: Certificates that clients cannot trust defeat the purpose of encryption and train staff to accept warnings; key and certificate management is the gap.

family: Legacy TLS and SSL (TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, SSLv2, SSLv3)
rationale: Deprecated protocol versions weaken the transport protection of guest and payment related data.

family: SWEET32, RC4 and weak key exchange ciphers
rationale: 3DES, RC4 and short Diffie-Hellman groups do not meet current strong cryptography expectations.

family: Remote access tools (remote control agents, VNC, RDP exposure)
rationale: Several overlapping remote tools widen the attack surface; remote access needs one controlled, authenticated and logged path.
Without NLA a session is offered before the user authenticates, which weakens secure logon and invites brute force.
A critical remote code execution flaw with a vendor fix shows patches are not applied within a defined time.

iso_control_title: Installation of software on operational systems
rationale: Software past vendor support or far behind current versions has no reliable security fixes, so lifecycle tracking is the gap.

family: Cleartext and insecure legacy protocols (FTP, SMTP, POP, IMAP, TFTP, NFS, rsync, SMBv1)
rationale: Guest and business data moved over cleartext or legacy services can be read or altered in transit; secure transfer rules are missing.

family: Legacy simple services and unneeded network responses
rationale: Echo, chargen, QOTD and finger have no business use on a hotel server; secure by default configuration removes them.

family: SSH weakness (weak ciphers, MACs, Terrapin, password logon)
rationale: Weak SSH algorithms and password logon on an administrative channel fall short of strong cryptography for remote administration.
